instructor: Mr. Ahmed is one of the greatest instructors I have ever crossed paths with. He perfectly manages to bond with the students and make them thrive in the lectures, not with force but with his developed communication skills. His strongest point is his ability to bond with us. As the weak part, I can't think of anything. Everything's just been great about him.
Enjoyable and fluency class but slightly lack of discipline in class

The instructor has some positive communication skills. He is friendly, polite, and approachable in class. His pronunciation and accent are clear, and he speaks fluently, which creates a comfortable classroom atmosphere. However, these strengths have not had a strong impact on my overall language development. There are several weaknesses that negatively affect the learning process. Moodle is not used actively or effectively, and the official coursebooks are rarely used during lessons. Instead, the instructor mainly relies on his own materials, which causes a lack of connection between the lessons, the coursebooks, and the curriculum. In addition, students are not clearly informed about curriculum progress, so we do not know which unit or topic we are currently studying unless we check it ourselves. In previous classes, this information was written on the board, which helped students follow the course more easily. Grammar and vocabulary topics are not supported with sufficient practice, and when practice is given, it is usually limited. Since the beginning of the course, I have had to rely mostly on my own efforts, which has been exhausting and has reduced my motivation. Lessons also tend to move away from the main topic, making it harder to stay focused and use class time effectively. Finally, vocabulary studies are insufficient, and there is no structured vocabulary program. At this level, I do not feel that I have learned enough from the course itself. Overall, the lack of structure, effective material use, and sufficient practice limits the effectiveness of the course and negatively affects student motivation.
course: The Upper course is too harsh on students. I think that the weight of this lecture can be shared with other levels - a lot of things are expected from us, despite the other levels. But of course, the weakest point of the PREP is ATTENDANCE. I assure you, as a student myself, that the harsh attendance rule makes us more distant to our classes. We should be able to miss more classes.

One of the strongest aspects of the course is the relaxed and low-stress classroom atmosphere. Lessons are generally comfortable, and students do not feel pressure while participating. This can be positive for speaking confidence and reduces anxiety for some learners. In addition, exposure to spoken English during class helps students become more familiar with listening to natural speech.
However, the weaknesses of the course are more significant. The course lacks clear structure and consistency. Moodle is not used actively, and course materials are not organized or followed systematically. The official coursebooks provided by the school are rarely used, which creates a disconnect between the curriculum and classroom instruction. As a result, it is difficult for students to understand how lessons fit into the overall program.
Another weak aspect is the lack of sufficient grammar and vocabulary practice. Topics are introduced but not reinforced with enough exercises. This forces students to rely mostly on their own efforts outside class. Over time, this reduces motivation and makes students feel that they are not learning enough from the course itself. Overall, the course does not provide enough guidance, practice, or structure to support effective language development.
